Question

Was this introduced once, or several times?

Tell apart a single introduction followed by local spread from repeated introductions from elsewhere.

This question can only be answered with context. A tree built from local samples alone cannot show whether they came in once or several times, so the protocol must include genomes from outside the investigation.

Which protocol to use

Choose the group your pathogen belongs to.

If the pathogen is Viruses

  1. Viral phylogenomic surveillance

Include background genomes from outside your area, for example from public databases. Local cases that form one clade suggest a single introduction. Local cases interleaved with outside genomes suggest several.

If the pathogen is Bacteria

  1. Bacterial phylogenomic surveillance

Include background isolates of the same lineage from other places. Several distinct clusters of local isolates, each closer to outside isolates than to each other, suggest repeated introductions.

If the pathogen is Fungi

  1. Fungal phylogenomic surveillance

Include background isolates from other places and, where relevant, other clades of the species. Local isolates from different clades indicate separate introductions.
